facts: get_block_2d_copy_D delegates to make_block_2d_copy_D for void CopyOp (1823-1830).
The destination engine's value type flows to the D selector; MMA::ValTypeD supplies the accumulator type (1116-1123, 1152-1163).
For float memory and float D, block_2d_selector chooses CopyBits=32 and XE_STORE_2D<32,...> (827-886).
The D store traits pass the 32-bit register fragment and coordinate payload to the selected store atom (500-543).
The surface descriptor derives width, height and pitch from the destination tensor; byte limits and alignment are documented and optionally asserted (110-128).
The base atom permits 8/16/32/64-bit elements and enforces width and height limits (54-68).
XE_STORE_2D has store height <=8 and emits lsc_store_block2d with its Bits template parameter (979-1025).

corrections.finding: The report says the pinned TLA public material does not prove that get_block_2d_copy_D accepts a 32-bit destination or emits d32. Exact pinned headers prove source-level support: float destination and ValTypeD=float select XE_STORE_2D<32,...>, whose typed store emits the block-2D d32 form.
corrections.evidence: Revision 87f6850680a580654b9ea2c80dbc01aeb36ad231; hashes and line references recorded under source_facts and in research-round1038-review-v1.txt.
corrections.action: Remove the d32 helper-support uncertainty from retrieval metadata. Retain compile/AOT/ISA/runtime qualification and typed float rectangle safety gates.

corrections.finding: A compiler or device qualification failure for block-2D does not imply an all-or-nothing blocker; ordinary typed SYCL scalar stores can be an explicit FP32 epilogue, with vectorization evaluated after lane ownership and bounds are correct.
corrections.evidence: SYCL typed pointer stores are an available kernel mechanism; this is a fallback design candidate, not a measured or implemented route.
corrections.action: Keep the typed block-2D route first. If its target qualification fails, evaluate a bounded scalar epilogue before considering the extra conversion pass.
